rationale: C17 is a highly specific predecessor template: both proclamations identify an earlier bilateral trade agreement under section 350(a), name the proclamations that implemented it, recite a bilateral agreement terminating the trade agreement on a specified date, state the President's statutory authority to terminate implementing proclamations, and then terminate those proclamations on that date. Their wording and recital-to-operative sequence are exceptionally close, with Uruguay, dates, and the extension statute substituted for Turkey and its corresponding details. C21 and C06 use the same machinery but are slightly less exact because each concerns only one implementing proclamation and uses somewhat different termination predicates or formulations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the President of the United States entered into a trade agreement with the President of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay on July 21, 1942 ... and proclaimed such trade agreement by proclamations of November 10, 1942 ... and December 3, 1942
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the President of the United States entered into a trade agreement with the President of the Turkish Republic on April 1, 1939 ... and proclaimed such trade agreement by proclamations of April 5, 1939 ... and November 30, 1939
shared_material.explanation: Distinctively parallel opening recital naming the bilateral agreement and two implementing proclamations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: pursuant to an agreement reached by the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Oriental Republic of Uruguay providing for the termination of the said trade agreement, such trade agreement ceased to have effect on December 28, 1953
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Turkey have agreed to terminate the said trade agreement, effective August 4, 1952
shared_material.explanation: The same bilateral-agreement termination predicate is adapted to a different country and effective date.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the said section 350 (a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 authorizes the President to terminate in whole or in part any proclamation carrying out a trade agreement entered into under such section
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the said section 350(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 authorizes the President to terminate in whole or in part any proclamation carrying out a trade agreement entered into under such section
shared_material.explanation: Nearly verbatim statement of the specific termination authority.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do proclaim that the said proclamations dated November 10, 1942, and December 3, 1942, are hereby terminated as of December 28, 1953
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby proclaim that the said proclamations dated April 5, 1939, and November 30, 1939, shall terminate August 4, 1952
shared_material.explanation: Closely matching operative disposition terminating two named proclamations on the agreed date.
